beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Minimum due, $150. Rohan pays it, on time, every month. Keep that up, and his balance of $5,000 costs him $11,638.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Wait. I never miss a payment. How can it cost that much?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because at that pace, every dinner and every gadget on this card ends up costing about 2.3× its price.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And he is far from alone. Millions of people do exactly this. The bill is paid, nothing is late, and it feels responsible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So in the next few minutes: how long the minimum really takes, how much it really costs, and the one line on your statement that fixes it.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Paying the minimum is like running on a treadmill, Rohan. You work hard every month, and the belt keeps pulling you back.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The belt is interest. His card charges 1.85% a month on whatever he still owes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That sounds small. But over a year it adds up to 22.2%. And because interest is charged on interest, it really works out to about 25%.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Okay, but I pay $150 every single month. That has to add up to something.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here is how that minimum is worked out. It is a small slice of the balance, 3% on this card. Owed, $5,000. Minimum, $150.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So he pays. Then interest lands on everything that is left, and a big part of his payment simply leaks back out as next month's interest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now the sneaky part. As the balance shrinks, the minimum shrinks with it. His steps get smaller, right when he should be speeding up.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The minimum is not built to get you out. It is built to keep you in.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Twelve months go by. Rohan pays the minimum every single time. Never late, not once.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By now, he has paid $1,685. And he still owes $4,323.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: I paid all that, and I still owe that much?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because $1,008 of what he paid went straight to the bank as interest. Only the rest touched the actual debt.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: And Rohan? That was the good year.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From here, the road gets long. A new year, a new signpost, and the balance is still walking right beside him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here is the whole journey if he keeps paying only the minimum. Red is what he still owes. Green is everything he has paid.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Look how the red line flattens out. The smaller the balance, the smaller the minimum, so the last stretch drags on for years.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In total, it takes 199 monthly payments. That is about 17 years.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Years? I will be paying this off longer than I have been working!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By the time this card is cleared, Rohan could change jobs, move cities, maybe start a family. And still be paying for this year's shopping.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: All in, he pays $11,638 to clear $5,000. And $6,638 of that is pure interest.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: In my bank days, we had a name for people who paid only the minimum. Our best customers. They never complained, and they never left.

lines.text: New buys: interest from day one

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And our maths is the kind version. Real cards charge interest daily, on the balance before your payment lands. And keep using the card, and new purchases charge interest from day one.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So the real bill is even bigger?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Usually, yes. So stop playing their game. Change one rule.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Same card. Same $5,000. Same rate. One change. Instead of the minimum, Rohan picks one fixed payment, and never lets it shrink.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: To clear the whole balance in three years, that payment is $191 a month.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His very first minimum was $150. The fixed payment is $191. A bigger step, but not a giant leap.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: That's it? I can find that.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: The trick is that it never shrinks. Same big step on the treadmill every month, while the belt keeps slowing down.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: As the balance falls, interest has less to chew on. So more of every payment hits the debt, and the debt falls faster and faster.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: 36 payments. And then it is gone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now the two roads, side by side. Minimum only: about 17 years, and $6,638 in interest. The fixed payment: three years, and $1,893.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Same debt, same rate. The minimum road costs $11,638 in total. The fixed road, $6,893.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Years sooner, and thousands less? Why did nobody tell me?

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Somebody did. It is printed on your statement, every single month.

lines.text: If you make only the minimum payment each period,
you will pay more in interest
and it will take you longer to pay off your balance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In the US, card statements carry a minimum payment warning. It shows how long you will be paying if you pay only the minimum, and what it will cost in total.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: For a balance like this one, there is a second line. The monthly payment that clears it in three years, and what that would cost.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: That number is the fix. No calculator needed. The card company has already done the maths for you.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Found it. It has been sitting there every month.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: One. Find the three year payment on the statement, and set autopay for that amount. Not the minimum.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Two. Stop adding new spending to this card while he clears it. Otherwise the belt speeds up again.

items.text: No new spending on this card

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Three. In a good month, pay a little extra. Every extra dollar goes straight at the balance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: One honest catch. If even that payment does not fit the budget, keep paying at least the minimum. A missed payment brings late fees, and can push the rate even higher.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: And then pick up the phone. Ask the card company for a lower rate or a payment plan. Asking costs nothing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So, two roads. Minimum only: about 17 years and $11,638. One fixed payment: 36 months and $6,893.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Autopay set. Fixed payment, not the minimum. And for the first time, this card has a finish line.

params.cta: On a US card? Find the three year line
params.assumption: Assumes 22.2% a year charged monthly, a minimum of 3% of the balance and no new spending. Real card formulas and fees differ.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Our maths is simplified, so real cards usually cost a bit more. Follow the panchayat for one money question, settled with real maths.
